summary.text: David Valadao is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for California's 22nd District. A Hanford dairy farmer and the son of Portuguese immigrants, he served in the California Assembly before his first election to Congress in 2012; he lost in 2018 and won the seat back in 2020. His campaign website says he will focus on water, costs, jobs and job training, and benefits for seniors and veterans.

paragraphs.text: Born April 14, 1977, and raised in Hanford, California, where his family, who emigrated from the Azores Islands of Portugal in 1969, started a dairy farm in 1973. According to his House biography, the family business now includes two dairies and more than 1,000 acres of farmland in Kings County.
Graduated from Hanford High School in 1995 and attended College of the Sequoias in Visalia.

Worked on his family's dairy farm and served as Regional Leadership Council Chairman for Land O'Lakes Inc.; his House biography says he has held leadership roles in dairy organizations and cooperatives.
Elected to the California State Assembly (30th District) in 2010 and served from 2010 to 2012, including as Vice-Chair of the Agriculture Committee.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2012 to represent California's 21st District and served from 2013 to 2019. He lost the 2018 election to TJ Cox and returned to the House after winning the 2020 election.

Represents California's 22nd District after redistricting; in the 2025-2026 Congress he sits on the House Appropriations Committee, where he chairs the Legislative Branch Subcommittee and also serves on the Defense and Agriculture subcommittees. His House biography says he has served on Appropriations throughout his time in Congress.
According to his House biography, he has focused on agriculture and water policy affecting the Central Valley. He and his wife Terra, whom he married in 1999, have three children, the biography says.
His campaign website says he will 'protect our water, put an end to out-of-control inflation and outrageous gas prices, work to bring new jobs and job training to the Central Valley.'
